detailed_summary: This paper generalizes the construction of two-block group algebra (2BGA) quantum LDPC codes by using the action of a group on the cosets of its subgroup, replacing the regular group actions of earlier constructions. This significantly expands the search space and yields new quantum LDPC codes outside the 2BGA family. Through computer search, the authors identify several new codes, including weight-6 codes with parameters [[48,8,6]], [[96,8,10]], [[224,12,16]] and weight-8 codes with parameters [[84,16,8]], [[112,16,10]], [[128,16,12]], [[168,16,15]]. They also introduce a maximally packed syndrome extraction schedule of depth w+2 for any code with maximum stabilizer weight w from their family. Under a standard circuit-level noise model, these codes perform competitively with BB codes when decoded using BP-OSD, achieving thresholds of approximately 0.65% for the weight-6 family and 0.35% for the weight-8 family. Finally, a group-theoretic framework is introduced to generate sequences of graph-based covers of 2BGA codes, recovering and extending recent results.
key_contributions: Generalization of 2BGA codes using group action on cosets of a subgroup, expanding the search space for quantum LDPC codes.
Introduction of a maximally packed syndrome extraction schedule of depth w+2 for codes with maximum stabilizer weight w.
Demonstration of competitive thresholds (≈0.65% for weight-6, ≈0.35% for weight-8) under circuit-level noise with BP-OSD decoding.
A group-theoretic framework for generating sequences of graph-based covers of 2BGA codes, extending prior results.
methodology_analysis: The authors generalize the construction of 2BGA codes by replacing regular group actions with the action of a group on the cosets of its subgroup. This allows for a broader class of codes, as the subgroup structure introduces more flexibility. They perform a computer search over small groups and subgroups to find codes with good parameters. For syndrome extraction, they design a schedule that reuses ancilla qubits in a maximally packed manner, achieving depth w+2 (including initialization and measurement). The decoding uses belief propagation with ordered statistics post-processing (BP-OSD) under a standard circuit-level noise model. The group-theoretic framework for covers is based on constructing sequences of graphs that are covers of the original Tanner graph, using group homomorphisms.
results_analysis: The paper reports several new quantum LDPC codes with parameters that improve over known codes. For weight-6, the [[48,8,6]] code has a rate of 1/6 and distance 6; the [[96,8,10]] code has rate 1/12 and distance 10; the [[224,12,16]] code has rate 3/56 and distance 16. For weight-8, the [[84,16,8]] code has rate 4/21 and distance 8; the [[112,16,10]] code has rate 1/7 and distance 10; the [[128,16,12]] code has rate 1/8 and distance 12; the [[168,16,15]] code has rate 2/21 and distance 15. Under circuit-level noise, the weight-6 family achieves a threshold of approximately 0.65%, and the weight-8 family achieves approximately 0.35%. These thresholds are competitive with BB codes, which are a leading family of quantum LDPC codes. The syndrome extraction schedule of depth w+2 is optimal in terms of depth for a given weight w, as it uses the minimum number of time steps.
strengths: The generalization of 2BGA codes is novel and significantly expands the search space for quantum LDPC codes.
The discovered codes have good parameters, including high distances relative to block length, and competitive thresholds under circuit-level noise.
The maximally packed syndrome extraction schedule is efficient and practical for implementation.
The group-theoretic framework for covers provides a systematic way to generate larger codes from smaller ones.
limitations: The computer search is limited to small groups and subgroups, so the codes found may not be optimal for larger parameters.
The thresholds are lower than some other families (e.g., surface codes have higher thresholds), but the codes have higher rates.
The paper does not provide a rigorous proof of the distance bounds for the new codes; they are found via search.
connections_to_research: This work directly advances quantum error correction, a key area in quantum physics. The construction of new quantum LDPC codes with good parameters and efficient syndrome extraction is crucial for building fault-tolerant quantum computers. The use of group theory connects to algebraic structures in quantum information, and the competitive thresholds under circuit-level noise demonstrate practical relevance. The paper also contributes to the theory of quantum codes by generalizing known constructions.
overall_assessment: This paper makes a significant contribution to the field of quantum error correction by generalizing the construction of two-block group algebra codes and discovering new quantum LDPC codes with competitive parameters. The introduction of a maximally packed syndrome extraction schedule and a group-theoretic framework for covers are valuable additions. The results are well-supported by computer searches and simulations. While the thresholds are not the highest, the codes offer higher rates and good distances, making them promising for practical applications. The paper is well-written and technically sound, representing a solid advance in quantum LDPC code design.
